digest.component_or_area: store write lock ownership and staleness detection
propositions: On platforms without /proc (macOS), _process_start_time always returns None, causing recycled-pid detection to fail and creating unbounded lock wedges when a dead process's pid is reused by an unrelated live process

_mkdir_lock_is_stale incorrectly treats a live-but-unrelated pid as proof of continued ownership when current_start cannot be determined, bypassing the 1h stale ceiling that otherwise bounds orphaned locks

The fix applies _mkdir_lock_age_exceeds_ceiling on the live-pid branch only when current_start is unavailable (unqualified verdict), preserving the never-break-a-corroborated-live-owner guarantee while bounding orphans

Lock ownership and staleness logic was extracted from lock.py (798/800 LOC) to a new lock_owner.py module to meet the 800 LOC hard cap, with one-way dependency and no re-export shim to ensure behavior-preserving refactoring
